newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity little changed on mild weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity little changed on mild weather.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were little changed at midday Monday with Palo Verde futures rising slightly in thin trade in forecasts for mild weather through the West, industry sources said.
"It's pretty quiet today," said one Houston-based futures trader, adding, "the weather in the West looks pretty bearish all week."

As of 1215 EDT, NYMEX July Palo Verde (PV) was up eight cents at the day's high of $28.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) following trade as low as $27.50, while August PV was up nine cents at the day's high of $31.20 after trades as low as $31.10 per MWh.

July California Oregon Border (COB) was up eight cents at the day's high of $17.50 after reaching as low as $17.05, while August was down seven cents at the day's low of $22.00 after exchange as high as $22.10 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1140 EDT an estimated total of 74 COB and 74 PV contracts had traded.

Weather forecasts called for near normal temperatures through much of the week in the Southwest with little precipation expected. Temperatures were expected to fall to just below normal late in the week.
In Phoenix, Ariz., the maximum temperature was expected to reach 102 degrees Fahrenheit Tuesday with an overnight low tonight expected near 74 degrees, Weather Services Corp said.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to average near normal then fall to a few degrees cooler than normal by the end of the week. Above-normal rainfall was expected through much of the area through the week.
In the West, the 1,221 MW Palo Verde unit 2 was reduced to 86 percent of capacity as of early Monday to repair a main feedwater heater leak, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.
The 550 MW unit 1 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired power plant in Wyoming was restarted over the weekend, as expected, sources familiar with the plant's operations said Monday.
The unit had been down since last Wednesday for unplanned repairs. Bridger's other three 550 MW units were said to be operating normally.
Other generation units were also expected to return to service as utilities ended spring maintenance and refueling outages in preparation for summer service.

Peak physical power at COB for Tuesday delivery was said to be talked near $13.50 from a range of $11.50-13.50 on Friday for Monday delivery, while Tuesday PV was talked at near $23.00 from $21.00-23.00 on Friday, sources said.
As of 1215 EDT, NYMEX July Henry Hub natural gas futures were down 2.8 cents at $2.16 per million British thermal units.
COB open interest for June 6 rose 333 to 6,465, while PV open interest rose 38 to 6,675, NYMEX said.
